#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: eb_emit_event timestamp platform fix and single-jq payload accumulation (#1806).
#   [#1806/SPEC-1] well-formed timestamp when ZBUILD_PLATFORM=linux + OSTYPE=darwin*
#   [#1806/SPEC-2] single jq invocation for payload; byte-identical output for same inputs
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "event-bus: timestamp platform fix and single-jq payload (#1806)"
setup_test_env "event-bus-timestamp"

EVENT_BUS="$REPO_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
REAL_DATE="$(command -v date)"
REAL_JQ="$(command -v jq)"
mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"

# ─── SPEC-1 [#1806/SPEC-1]: well-formed timestamp on darwin host + linux platform ──
print_test_section "SPEC-1 [#1806/SPEC-1]: no literal %3N when OSTYPE=darwin* ZBUILD_PLATFORM=linux"

# BSD/macOS date does not support %3N — it outputs the literal characters %3N.
# This mock simulates that behaviour so the test runs on Linux CI.
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/date" <<MOCK
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for _arg in "\$@"; do
    case "\$_arg" in
        +*%3N*) printf '2026-01-01T12:00:00.%%3NZ\n'; exit 0 ;;
    esac
done
exec $REAL_DATE "\$@"
MOCK
chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/date"
export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin:$PATH"

_S1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1"
mkdir -p "$_S1"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$_S1/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="/dev/null"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$_S1"
: > "$_S1/events.jsonl"

# Simulate: macOS host (OSTYPE=darwin*) with ZBUILD_PLATFORM=linux.
# Old code checked ZBUILD_PLATFORM == "macos"; on Linux CI ZBUILD_PLATFORM=linux,
# so old code went to the else branch and called date with %3N, producing the
# literal string %3N on a macOS host.  New code checks OSTYPE.
OSTYPE="darwin12.3.0"
unset _ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_LOADED _ZBUILD_EVENT_KNOWN_TYPES_LOADED 2>/dev/null || true
# shellcheck source=../../core/event-bus/event-bus.sh
source "$EVENT_BUS"

eb_emit_event "pipeline.start" "run_id=test-1806" "issue=1806"

_ts="$(jq -r '.ts // empty' "$_S1/events.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "$_ts" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-1] event emitted to events.jsonl" "file empty or ts missing"
else
    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-1] event emitted to events.jsonl"
fi

if grep -qF '%3N' "$_S1/events.jsonl" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-1] timestamp must not contain literal %3N" "ts: $_ts"
else
    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-1] timestamp contains no literal %3N"
fi

# Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.NNNz  (3 decimal digits, Z or z)
if [[ "$_ts" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{3}[Zz]$ ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-1] timestamp is well-formed ISO 8601 with milliseconds"
else
    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-1] timestamp is well-formed ISO 8601 with milliseconds" \
        "got: $_ts"
fi

# ─── SPEC-2 [#1806/SPEC-2]: single jq invocation; byte-identical payload output ──
print_test_section "SPEC-2 [#1806/SPEC-2]: single jq call accumulates all key=val args"

JQ_CALL_LOG="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/jq-calls.log"
export JQ_CALL_LOG
: > "$JQ_CALL_LOG"

# Wrap the real jq to record every invocation; real jq still executes so output
# is preserved and the payload-identity assertion has something to check.
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/jq" <<MOCK
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "\${JQ_CALL_LOG:-/dev/null}"
exec $REAL_JQ "\$@"
MOCK
chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/jq"

_S2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s2"
mkdir -p "$_S2"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$_S2/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$_S2"
: > "$_S2/events.jsonl"

# Restore a non-darwin OSTYPE so the timestamp goes through the Linux path
# (date supports %3N on Linux; the mock date is still on PATH but is not called
# for non-%3N formats — it falls through to exec the real date).
OSTYPE="linux-gnu"
unset _ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_LOADED _ZBUILD_EVENT_KNOWN_TYPES_LOADED 2>/dev/null || true
source "$EVENT_BUS"

: > "$JQ_CALL_LOG"
eb_emit_event "stage.complete" "stage=test-stage" "verdict=pass" "extra=data-value"

# Old code called jq once per key=val argument with the filter '. + {($k): $v}'.
# New code accumulates all args and calls jq once — that per-arg filter is gone.
_loop_calls="$(grep -cF '{($k): $v}' "$JQ_CALL_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ "$_loop_calls" -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-2] per-arg accumulation pattern '. + {(\$k): \$v}' absent"
else
    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-2] per-arg accumulation pattern absent" \
        "found $_loop_calls call(s) with old per-arg filter"
fi

# All key=val args must survive in the payload (byte-identical output check)
_ev="$(cat "$_S2/events.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1806/SPEC-2] payload.stage preserved" "test-stage" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.stage // empty' <<< "$_ev" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1806/SPEC-2] payload.verdict preserved" "pass" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.verdict // empty' <<< "$_ev" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1806/SPEC-2] payload.extra preserved" "data-value" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.extra // empty' <<< "$_ev" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1806/SPEC-2] event type preserved" "stage.complete" \
    "$(jq -r '.type // empty' <<< "$_ev" 2>/dev/null || true)"

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: the run-status comment sidecar as a PROCESS (#2131, ADR-064).
3	#
4	# Drives a live events.jsonl and watches the recording `gh`: no call before
5	# pipeline.start, the start row lands before any stage, bursts coalesce, a
6	# terminal event flushes at once but does not end the process (always-run
7	# stages emit after pipeline.end — the runner's trap reaps us), TERM and
8	# parent death both end with a final render.
9	set -uo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
12	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
13	
14	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
15	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
16	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
17	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
18	
19	print_test_header "run-status-comment — sidecar loop (#2131)"
20	setup_test_env "rsc-loop"
21	
22	LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
23	GH_LOG="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/gh.log"; GH_BODIES="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bodies"; mkdir -p "$GH_BODIES"
24	cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh" <<MOCK
25	#!/usr/bin/env bash
26	args="\$*"
27	# Body first, log line second: a test that waits on the log must find the body already there.
28	case "\$args" in *body=@*) f="\${args##*body=@}"; f="\${f%% *}"; n="\$(ls "$GH_BODIES" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; cp "\$f" "$GH_BODIES/body-\$((n+1)).txt" ;; esac
29	printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$GH_LOG"
30	case "\$args" in
31	  "auth status"*) exit 0 ;;
32	  *--paginate*) echo '[]'; exit 0 ;;
33	  *"-X PATCH"*) echo '{}'; exit 0 ;;
34	  *issues/*/comments*) echo 4242; exit 0 ;;
35	esac
36	exit 1
37	MOCK
38	chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh"
39	
40	export ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=2
41	export ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_POLL=0.2
42	export ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT=5
43	unset NO_GITHUB
44	
45	ev() {   # ev <events> <time> <type> [seq] [stage] [k=v...]
46	    local f="$1" t="$2" type="$3" seq="${4:-}" stage="${5:-}"; shift 5
47	    local data="{}" kv
48	    for kv in "$@"; do data="$(jq -c --arg k "${kv%%=*}" --arg v "${kv#*=}" '. + {($k): $v}' <<< "$data")"; done
49	    jq -cn --arg ts "2026-09-17T${t}.000Z" --arg type "$type" --arg seq "$seq" --arg stage "$stage" --argjson data "$data" \
50	        '{ts:$ts, run_id:"r-loop", issue:90000042, type:$type, plugin:"", kind:"", data:$data, schema_version:1}
51	         + (if $stage != "" then {stage:$stage} else {} end) + (if $seq != "" then {seq:$seq} else {} end)' >> "$f"
52	}
53	posts() { grep -c -E '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' "$GH_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true; }
54	patches() { grep -c -- '-X PATCH' "$GH_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true; }
55	last_body() { ls "$GH_BODIES"/body-*.txt 2>/dev/null | sort -t- -k2 -n | tail -1 | xargs cat 2>/dev/null; }
56	# #2191-class flake: the gh stub logs the PATCH line and copies its body in two
57	# steps, so "a PATCH was logged" does not mean "the body we want is there" — an
58	# earlier interval PATCH can land first. Wait for the body that says <text>.
59	wait_for_body() {   # <text> <tries> <interval>
60	    local i
61	    for (( i = 0; i < ${2:-50}; i++ )); do
62	        grep -qF -- "$1" <<< "$(last_body)" && return 0
63	        sleep "${3:-0.1}"
64	    done
65	    return 1
66	}
67	alive() { kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
68	wait_gone() { local i; for (( i=0; i<50; i++ )); do alive "$1" || return 0; sleep 0.1; done; return 1; }
69	
70	start_sidecar() {   # start_sidecar <state_dir> <parent_pid> → pid (a child of THIS shell, so `wait` works)
71	    bash "$LIB" --events "$1/events.jsonl" --state-dir "$1" --parent-pid "$2" \
72	        --slug testuser/testrepo --issue 90000042 --run-id r-loop >>"$1/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
73	    pid=$!
74	}
75	
76	# ─── SPEC-1: nothing before pipeline.start; then the start row lands ───────
77	S1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1"; mkdir -p "$S1"; : > "$S1/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"
78	sleep 3600 & PARENT=$!
79	start_sidecar "$S1" "$PARENT"
80	sleep 1
81	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] no gh call while events.jsonl is empty" "0" "$(posts)"
82	ev "$S1/events.jsonl" 12:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
83	if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1; then
84	    assert_pass "[SPEC-1] pipeline.start → POST within 3s (the run is visible before any stage)"
85	else
86	    assert_fail "[SPEC-1] pipeline.start → POST within 3s" "log: $(cat "$GH_LOG" 2>/dev/null)"
87	fi
88	assert_contains "[SPEC-1] posted body carries the marker" "$(last_body)" 'zbuild-run-status run_id=r-loop'
89	assert_contains "[SPEC-1] posted body header says running" "$(last_body)" '**running**'
90	
91	# ─── SPEC-2: a burst coalesces ──────────────────────────────────────────────
92	: > "$GH_LOG"
93	for i in 1 2 3; do
94	    ev "$S1/events.jsonl" "12:0$i:00" plugin.run.start "$i" "s$i" plugin="s$i" kind=tool
95	    ev "$S1/events.jsonl" "12:0$i:30" stage.complete "$i" "s$i" stage="s$i" verdict=pass
96	done
97	# Wait for the body that shows the newest row, not a fixed sleep: under coverage
98	# tracing the sidecar is several times slower (#2191-class flake, CI 2026-09-25).
99	wait_for_body '**3 s3**' 200 0.1 || true
100	n="$(patches)"
101	# Coalescing means fewer PATCHes than events — on a slow runner the burst can
102	# straddle an interval, so the bound is "not one per event", not "1–2".
103	if [[ "$n" -ge 1 && "$n" -lt 6 ]]; then
104	    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] 6 events in a burst → $n PATCH(es), not 6"
105	else
106	    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] 6 events in a burst coalesce" "got $n PATCHes"
107	fi
108	assert_contains "[SPEC-2] the latest PATCH has the newest row on top" "$(last_body | grep -E '^\*\*' | sed -n 1p)" '**3 s3**'
109	
110	# ─── SPEC-3: an open row survives a KILL of the sidecar ─────────────────────
111	ev "$S1/events.jsonl" 12:10:00 plugin.run.start 4 build plugin=build kind=agent
112	wait_for_body '**4 build**' 200 0.1 || true   # posted, however slow the runner
113	kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
114	assert_contains "[SPEC-3] the body on GitHub already had the running row (start before end)" "$(last_body)" '**8:10 AM ET → running** · **4 build**'
115	
116	# ─── SPEC-4: terminal flushes immediately and the process stays alive ──────
117	# This sidecar's gap between edits is an hour, so the only way an edit can
118	# follow pipeline.end is the flush-at-once rule — the wait can then be generous
119	# without weakening the check. (It used to sleep past a 2 s gap and demand an
120	# edit within 1.5 s: an ordinary timed edit passed it, and suite load failed it
121	# — #2258.)
122	S2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s2"; mkdir -p "$S2"; : > "$S2/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
123	ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
124	ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=3600 start_sidecar "$S2" "$PARENT"
125	wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1
126	ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:05 plugin.run.start 1 intake plugin=intake kind=agent
127	ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:06 stage.complete 1 intake stage=intake verdict=pass
128	: > "$GH_LOG"
129	ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:07 pipeline.end "" "" status=success run_id=r-loop issue=90000042
130	if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" 'X PATCH' 200 0.1; then
131	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] pipeline.end → PATCH without waiting out the gap between edits"
132	else
133	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] pipeline.end → PATCH without waiting out the gap between edits" "no PATCH"
134	fi
135	wait_for_body '**success**' 100 0.1 || true
136	assert_contains "[SPEC-4] final header says success" "$(last_body)" '**success**'
137	if alive "$pid"; then
138	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the sidecar is still alive after the terminal event (always-run stages come later)"
139	else
140	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the sidecar is still alive after the terminal event" "exited"
141	fi
142	# An always-run stage after pipeline.end: the hour-long gap holds its timed
143	# edit back, so SPEC-5's final render is where it must land.
144	ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:08 plugin.run.start 9 persist plugin=persist kind=tool
145	ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:09 stage.complete 9 persist stage=persist verdict=pass
146	
147	# ─── SPEC-5: TERM → final render, exit 0 ────────────────────────────────────
148	: > "$GH_LOG"
149	kill -TERM "$pid"
150	if wait_gone "$pid"; then
151	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
152	    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] TERM ends the sidecar within 5s"
153	    assert_eq "[SPEC-5] exit status 0 on TERM" "0" "$rc"
154	else
155	    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] TERM ends the sidecar within 5s" "still alive"; kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null
156	fi
157	assert_eq "[SPEC-5] TERM produced one final PATCH" "1" "$(patches)"
158	assert_contains "[SPEC-5] final body keeps the terminal status from the events" "$(last_body)" '**success**'
159	assert_contains "[SPEC-5] a stage after pipeline.end lands in the final render" "$(last_body)" '**9 persist**'
160	
161	# ─── SPEC-6: TERM before any terminal event → interrupted ───────────────────
162	S3="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3"; mkdir -p "$S3"; : > "$S3/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
163	ev "$S3/events.jsonl" 14:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
164	ev "$S3/events.jsonl" 14:00:01 plugin.run.start 1 build plugin=build kind=agent
165	start_sidecar "$S3" "$PARENT"
166	wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1
167	kill -TERM "$pid"; wait_gone "$pid"; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
168	assert_contains "[SPEC-6] no terminal event + TERM → interrupted" "$(last_body)" '**interrupted**'
169	assert_contains "[SPEC-6] the running row keeps its start" "$(last_body)" '**10:00 AM ET → running** · **1 build**'
170	
171	# ─── SPEC-7: parent death → final render, exit 0 ────────────────────────────
172	S4="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s4"; mkdir -p "$S4"; : > "$S4/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
173	ev "$S4/events.jsonl" 15:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
174	sleep 2 & SHORT=$!
175	start_sidecar "$S4" "$SHORT"
176	wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1
177	wait "$SHORT" 2>/dev/null
178	if wait_gone "$pid"; then
179	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
180	    assert_pass "[SPEC-7] parent death ends the sidecar"
181	    assert_eq "[SPEC-7] exit status 0 on parent death" "0" "$rc"
182	else
183	    assert_fail "[SPEC-7] parent death ends the sidecar" "still alive"; kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null
184	fi
185	assert_contains "[SPEC-7] final body names the cause" "$(last_body)" 'interrupted (runner exited without a terminal event)'
186	
187	# ─── SPEC-8: --once renders and exits ───────────────────────────────────────
188	: > "$GH_LOG"
189	bash "$LIB" --events "$S4/events.jsonl" --state-dir "$S4" --parent-pid $$ \
190	    --slug testuser/testrepo --issue 90000042 --run-id r-loop --once; rc=$?
191	assert_eq "[SPEC-8] --once exits 0" "0" "$rc"
192	assert_eq "[SPEC-8] --once made exactly one gh write" "1" "$(( $(posts) + $(patches) ))"
193	
194	# ─── SPEC-3 [#1806/SPEC-3]: last_size cursor updated after flush ─────────────
195	# After rsc_flush returns, the poll loop must update last_size to the current
196	# byte count of events.jsonl so that events written inside rsc_flush (e.g.
197	# redaction.applied via apply_scope_redaction) do not set dirty=1 and trigger
198	# a spurious second render.
199	S_SC3="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s_sc3"; mkdir -p "$S_SC3"; : > "$S_SC3/events.jsonl"
200	: > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
201	
202	# gh mock: during a PATCH call, inject a fake event so events.jsonl grows
203	# while last_size is still the pre-flush value (simulating redaction.applied).
204	cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh" <<MOCK
205	#!/usr/bin/env bash
206	args="\$*"
207	case "\$args" in *body=@*) f="\${args##*body=@}"; f="\${f%% *}"; n="\$(ls "$GH_BODIES" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; cp "\$f" "$GH_BODIES/body-\$((n+1)).txt" ;; esac
208	printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$GH_LOG"
209	case "\$args" in
210	  "auth status"*) exit 0 ;;
211	  *--paginate*) echo '[]'; exit 0 ;;
212	  *"-X PATCH"*)
213	    printf '%s\n' '{"ts":"2026-10-10T00:00:00.000Z","type":"redaction.applied","run_id":"r-loop","issue":90000042,"data":{},"schema_version":1}' >> "$S_SC3/events.jsonl"
214	    echo '{}'
215	    exit 0
216	    ;;
217	  *issues/*/comments*) echo 4242; exit 0 ;;
218	esac
219	exit 1
220	MOCK
221	chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh"
222	
223	ev "$S_SC3/events.jsonl" 23:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc engine_branch=main
224	ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=2 start_sidecar "$S_SC3" "$PARENT"
225	wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1 || true
226	ev "$S_SC3/events.jsonl" 23:00:01 stage.complete 1 build stage=build verdict=pass
227	
228	# Wait for the first PATCH; the mock injects a byte into events.jsonl during it.
229	if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" 'X PATCH' 30 0.1; then
230	    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-3] first PATCH fired"
231	else
232	    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-3] first PATCH fired (setup)" "no PATCH in GH_LOG"
233	fi
234	
235	# Reset: only count PATCHes that appear AFTER this point.
236	: > "$GH_LOG"
237	
238	# Old code: last_size was set before the flush, file grew during it → dirty=1
239	# next interval → second PATCH.  New code: cursor updated after flush → dirty=0
240	# → no second PATCH within MIN_INTERVAL * 1.5.
241	sleep 3
242	
243	_sc3_patches="$(patches)"
244	if [[ "$_sc3_patches" -eq 0 ]]; then
245	    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-3] no spurious PATCH after event injected during flush"
246	else
247	    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-3] no spurious PATCH after event injected during flush" \
248	        "got $_sc3_patches PATCH(es) — last_size cursor not updated after flush"
249	fi
250	kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
251	
252	# ─── SPEC-4 [#1806/SPEC-4]: no PATCH when rendered body is byte-for-byte identical ──
253	S_SC4="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s_sc4"; mkdir -p "$S_SC4"; : > "$S_SC4/events.jsonl"
254	: > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
255	
256	# Restore default gh mock (no injection).
257	cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh" <<MOCK
258	#!/usr/bin/env bash
259	args="\$*"
260	case "\$args" in *body=@*) f="\${args##*body=@}"; f="\${f%% *}"; n="\$(ls "$GH_BODIES" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; cp "\$f" "$GH_BODIES/body-\$((n+1)).txt" ;; esac
261	printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$GH_LOG"
262	case "\$args" in
263	  "auth status"*) exit 0 ;;
264	  *--paginate*) echo '[]'; exit 0 ;;
265	  *"-X PATCH"*) echo '{}'; exit 0 ;;
266	  *issues/*/comments*) echo 4242; exit 0 ;;
267	esac
268	exit 1
269	MOCK
270	chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh"
271	
272	ev "$S_SC4/events.jsonl" 23:30:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc engine_branch=main
273	ev "$S_SC4/events.jsonl" 23:30:01 stage.complete 1 build stage=build verdict=pass
274	ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=2 start_sidecar "$S_SC4" "$PARENT"
275	wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1 || true
276	
277	# Wait for the first PATCH (MIN_INTERVAL=2 after pipeline.start POST).
278	if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" 'X PATCH' 30 0.1; then
279	    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-4] first PATCH fired"
280	else
281	    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-4] first PATCH fired (setup)" "no PATCH in GH_LOG"
282	fi
283	
284	# Append an event that rsc_rows_json does not render — the body is unchanged.
285	: > "$GH_LOG"
286	printf '%s\n' '{"ts":"2026-10-10T00:00:01.000Z","type":"redaction.applied","run_id":"r-loop","issue":90000042,"data":{},"schema_version":1}' \
287	    >> "$S_SC4/events.jsonl"
288	
289	# Wait long enough for dirty=1 to be processed (file grew) and a second flush
290	# to fire if rsc_upsert is not guarded by a body comparison.
291	sleep 4
292	
293	_sc4_patches="$(patches)"
294	if [[ "$_sc4_patches" -eq 0 ]]; then
295	    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-4] no PATCH when rendered body is identical to previous flush"
296	else
297	    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-4] no PATCH when body is identical" \
298	        "got $_sc4_patches PATCH(es) — rsc_upsert was called with an unchanged body"
299	fi
300	kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
301	
302	# ─── SPEC-5 [#1806/SPEC-5]: sidecar events carry stage=run-status-comment ────
303	# Every emit_event call from the sidecar process must include stage=run-status-comment
304	# in the envelope.  In the old code emit_event is a no-op stub; in the new code
305	# the sidecar sources event-bus and exports ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE=run-status-comment.
306	S_SC5="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s_sc5"; mkdir -p "$S_SC5"; : > "$S_SC5/events.jsonl"
307	SC5_EVENTS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sc5-events.jsonl"; : > "$SC5_EVENTS"
308	: > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
309	
310	# scope-manifest.md triggers apply_scope_redaction during rsc_outbound_body;
311	# apply_scope_redaction calls emit_event("redaction.applied"), which (new code)
312	# writes to SC5_EVENTS.  "` + ./`" allows every path so redaction succeeds.
313	printf '+ ./\n' > "$S_SC5/scope-manifest.md"
314	
315	ev "$S_SC5/events.jsonl" 23:45:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc engine_branch=main
316	
317	# Start sidecar with its own ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL so its emits go to SC5_EVENTS
318	# and do not mix with the events.jsonl the sidecar reads.
319	ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$SC5_EVENTS" ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="/dev/null" ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR" \
320	ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=2 \
321	    bash "$LIB" --events "$S_SC5/events.jsonl" --state-dir "$S_SC5" --parent-pid "$PARENT" \
322	    --slug testuser/testrepo --issue 90000042 --run-id r-loop >>"$S_SC5/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
323	pid=$!
324	
325	# The first flush fires immediately (flushed_once=0); apply_scope_redaction runs
326	# and calls emit_event — must be in SC5_EVENTS before the POST is logged.
327	if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1; then
328	    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-5] initial POST fired (apply_scope_redaction ran)"
329	else
330	    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-5] initial POST fired" "no POST — apply_scope_redaction may have failed"
331	fi
332	
333	# Old code: emit_event is a stub → SC5_EVENTS stays empty → count == 0.
334	# New code: event-bus sourced + ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE=run-status-comment →
335	#           SC5_EVENTS has at least one event.
336	_sc5_event_count="$(grep -c '' "$SC5_EVENTS" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
337	if [[ "$_sc5_event_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
338	    assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-5] sidecar emitted at least one event to its events file"
339	else
340	    assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-5] sidecar emitted at least one event" \
341	        "SC5_EVENTS is empty — emit_event is still a stub"
342	fi
343	
344	# Every emitted event must carry stage="run-status-comment".
345	if [[ "$_sc5_event_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
346	    _sc5_bad="$(jq -c 'select(.stage != "run-status-comment")' "$SC5_EVENTS" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '' || true)"
347	    if [[ "$_sc5_bad" -eq 0 ]]; then
348	        assert_pass "[#1806/SPEC-5] all sidecar events carry stage=run-status-comment"
349	    else
350	        assert_fail "[#1806/SPEC-5] all sidecar events carry stage=run-status-comment" \
351	            "$_sc5_bad event(s) missing the field"
352	    fi
353	fi
354	kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
355	
356	kill "$PARENT" 2>/dev/null; wait "$PARENT" 2>/dev/null
357	cleanup_test_env
358	print_test_results
359	exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: the run-status comment sidecar as a PROCESS (#2131, ADR-064).
#
# Drives a live events.jsonl and watches the recording `gh`: no call before
# pipeline.start, the start row lands before any stage, bursts coalesce, a
# terminal event flushes at once but does not end the process (always-run
# stages emit after pipeline.end — the runner's trap reaps us), TERM and
# parent death both end with a final render.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-status-comment — sidecar loop (#2131)"
setup_test_env "rsc-loop"

LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
GH_LOG="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/gh.log"; GH_BODIES="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bodies"; mkdir -p "$GH_BODIES"
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh" <<MOCK
#!/usr/bin/env bash
args="\$*"
# Body first, log line second: a test that waits on the log must find the body already there.
case "\$args" in *body=@*) f="\${args##*body=@}"; f="\${f%% *}"; n="\$(ls "$GH_BODIES" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; cp "\$f" "$GH_BODIES/body-\$((n+1)).txt" ;; esac
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$GH_LOG"
case "\$args" in
  "auth status"*) exit 0 ;;
  *--paginate*) echo '[]'; exit 0 ;;
  *"-X PATCH"*) echo '{}'; exit 0 ;;
  *issues/*/comments*) echo 4242; exit 0 ;;
esac
exit 1
MOCK
chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh"

export ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=2
export ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_POLL=0.2
export ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT=5
unset NO_GITHUB

ev() {   # ev <events> <time> <type> [seq] [stage] [k=v...]
    local f="$1" t="$2" type="$3" seq="${4:-}" stage="${5:-}"; shift 5
    local data="{}" kv
    for kv in "$@"; do data="$(jq -c --arg k "${kv%%=*}" --arg v "${kv#*=}" '. + {($k): $v}' <<< "$data")"; done
    jq -cn --arg ts "2026-09-17T${t}.000Z" --arg type "$type" --arg seq "$seq" --arg stage "$stage" --argjson data "$data" \
        '{ts:$ts, run_id:"r-loop", issue:90000042, type:$type, plugin:"", kind:"", data:$data, schema_version:1}
         + (if $stage != "" then {stage:$stage} else {} end) + (if $seq != "" then {seq:$seq} else {} end)' >> "$f"
}
posts() { grep -c -E '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' "$GH_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true; }
patches() { grep -c -- '-X PATCH' "$GH_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true; }
last_body() { ls "$GH_BODIES"/body-*.txt 2>/dev/null | sort -t- -k2 -n | tail -1 | xargs cat 2>/dev/null; }
# #2191-class flake: the gh stub logs the PATCH line and copies its body in two
# steps, so "a PATCH was logged" does not mean "the body we want is there" — an
# earlier interval PATCH can land first. Wait for the body that says <text>.
wait_for_body() {   # <text> <tries> <interval>
    local i
    for (( i = 0; i < ${2:-50}; i++ )); do
        grep -qF -- "$1" <<< "$(last_body)" && return 0
        sleep "${3:-0.1}"
    done
    return 1
}
alive() { kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
wait_gone() { local i; for (( i=0; i<50; i++ )); do alive "$1" || return 0; sleep 0.1; done; return 1; }

start_sidecar() {   # start_sidecar <state_dir> <parent_pid> → pid (a child of THIS shell, so `wait` works)
    bash "$LIB" --events "$1/events.jsonl" --state-dir "$1" --parent-pid "$2" \
        --slug testuser/testrepo --issue 90000042 --run-id r-loop >>"$1/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
    pid=$!
}

# ─── SPEC-1: nothing before pipeline.start; then the start row lands ───────
S1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1"; mkdir -p "$S1"; : > "$S1/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"
sleep 3600 & PARENT=$!
start_sidecar "$S1" "$PARENT"
sleep 1
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] no gh call while events.jsonl is empty" "0" "$(posts)"
ev "$S1/events.jsonl" 12:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-1] pipeline.start → POST within 3s (the run is visible before any stage)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-1] pipeline.start → POST within 3s" "log: $(cat "$GH_LOG" 2>/dev/null)"
fi
assert_contains "[SPEC-1] posted body carries the marker" "$(last_body)" 'zbuild-run-status run_id=r-loop'
assert_contains "[SPEC-1] posted body header says running" "$(last_body)" '**running**'

# ─── SPEC-2: a burst coalesces ──────────────────────────────────────────────
: > "$GH_LOG"
for i in 1 2 3; do
    ev "$S1/events.jsonl" "12:0$i:00" plugin.run.start "$i" "s$i" plugin="s$i" kind=tool
    ev "$S1/events.jsonl" "12:0$i:30" stage.complete "$i" "s$i" stage="s$i" verdict=pass
done
# Wait for the body that shows the newest row, not a fixed sleep: under coverage
# tracing the sidecar is several times slower (#2191-class flake, CI 2026-09-25).
wait_for_body '**3 s3**' 200 0.1 || true
n="$(patches)"
# Coalescing means fewer PATCHes than events — on a slow runner the burst can
# straddle an interval, so the bound is "not one per event", not "1–2".
if [[ "$n" -ge 1 && "$n" -lt 6 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] 6 events in a burst → $n PATCH(es), not 6"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] 6 events in a burst coalesce" "got $n PATCHes"
fi
assert_contains "[SPEC-2] the latest PATCH has the newest row on top" "$(last_body | grep -E '^\*\*' | sed -n 1p)" '**3 s3**'

# ─── SPEC-3: an open row survives a KILL of the sidecar ─────────────────────
ev "$S1/events.jsonl" 12:10:00 plugin.run.start 4 build plugin=build kind=agent
wait_for_body '**4 build**' 200 0.1 || true   # posted, however slow the runner
kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
assert_contains "[SPEC-3] the body on GitHub already had the running row (start before end)" "$(last_body)" '**8:10 AM ET → running** · **4 build**'

# ─── SPEC-4: terminal flushes immediately and the process stays alive ──────
# This sidecar's gap between edits is an hour, so the only way an edit can
# follow pipeline.end is the flush-at-once rule — the wait can then be generous
# without weakening the check. (It used to sleep past a 2 s gap and demand an
# edit within 1.5 s: an ordinary timed edit passed it, and suite load failed it
# — #2258.)
S2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s2"; mkdir -p "$S2"; : > "$S2/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL=3600 start_sidecar "$S2" "$PARENT"
wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1
ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:05 plugin.run.start 1 intake plugin=intake kind=agent
ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:06 stage.complete 1 intake stage=intake verdict=pass
: > "$GH_LOG"
ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:07 pipeline.end "" "" status=success run_id=r-loop issue=90000042
if wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" 'X PATCH' 200 0.1; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] pipeline.end → PATCH without waiting out the gap between edits"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] pipeline.end → PATCH without waiting out the gap between edits" "no PATCH"
fi
wait_for_body '**success**' 100 0.1 || true
assert_contains "[SPEC-4] final header says success" "$(last_body)" '**success**'
if alive "$pid"; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the sidecar is still alive after the terminal event (always-run stages come later)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the sidecar is still alive after the terminal event" "exited"
fi
# An always-run stage after pipeline.end: the hour-long gap holds its timed
# edit back, so SPEC-5's final render is where it must land.
ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:08 plugin.run.start 9 persist plugin=persist kind=tool
ev "$S2/events.jsonl" 13:00:09 stage.complete 9 persist stage=persist verdict=pass

# ─── SPEC-5: TERM → final render, exit 0 ────────────────────────────────────
: > "$GH_LOG"
kill -TERM "$pid"
if wait_gone "$pid"; then
    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] TERM ends the sidecar within 5s"
    assert_eq "[SPEC-5] exit status 0 on TERM" "0" "$rc"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] TERM ends the sidecar within 5s" "still alive"; kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null
fi
assert_eq "[SPEC-5] TERM produced one final PATCH" "1" "$(patches)"
assert_contains "[SPEC-5] final body keeps the terminal status from the events" "$(last_body)" '**success**'
assert_contains "[SPEC-5] a stage after pipeline.end lands in the final render" "$(last_body)" '**9 persist**'

# ─── SPEC-6: TERM before any terminal event → interrupted ───────────────────
S3="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3"; mkdir -p "$S3"; : > "$S3/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
ev "$S3/events.jsonl" 14:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
ev "$S3/events.jsonl" 14:00:01 plugin.run.start 1 build plugin=build kind=agent
start_sidecar "$S3" "$PARENT"
wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1
kill -TERM "$pid"; wait_gone "$pid"; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
assert_contains "[SPEC-6] no terminal event + TERM → interrupted" "$(last_body)" '**interrupted**'
assert_contains "[SPEC-6] the running row keeps its start" "$(last_body)" '**10:00 AM ET → running** · **1 build**'

# ─── SPEC-7: parent death → final render, exit 0 ────────────────────────────
S4="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s4"; mkdir -p "$S4"; : > "$S4/events.jsonl"; : > "$GH_LOG"; rm -f "$GH_BODIES"/*
ev "$S4/events.jsonl" 15:00:00 pipeline.start "" "" run_id=r-loop issue=90000042 engine_sha=abc1234 engine_branch=main
sleep 2 & SHORT=$!
start_sidecar "$S4" "$SHORT"
wait_for_event "$GH_LOG" '^api repos/testuser/testrepo/issues/90000042/comments' 30 0.1
wait "$SHORT" 2>/dev/null
if wait_gone "$pid"; then
    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
    assert_pass "[SPEC-7] parent death ends the sidecar"
    assert_eq "[SPEC-7] exit status 0 on parent death" "0" "$rc"

7	# run execs ~6,600 external processes; `source runner.sh` alone execs 1,375.

10	# as plugin-event-balance-full-run-test.sh) under bash xtrace and counts every
11	# external command the engine and its children exec. The count must stay under
12	# FORK_BUDGET, which only ratchets DOWN (raising it needs an ADR-065 amendment).
13	# The failure output IS the diagnosis: the top call sites and per-file totals.

111	            tag = (site in ex) ? "\tX" : ""
112	            n = split(site, sp, "/"); site = sp[n]
113	            line = $0; sub(/^\++@[^@]*@ /, "", line)

117	                if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/) {                  # VAR=val prefix

233	echo "  external execs: $_total (budget $FORK_BUDGET) across $_files source files"
234	echo "  top call sites:"
235	awk -F'\t' 'NR <= 12 { printf "    %5d  %-34s %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }' "$SITES"
236	if [[ -s "$SITES.exempt" ]]; then
237	    echo "  exempt waits (not counted — their repeat count is elapsed time):"
238	    awk -F'\t' '{ printf "    %5d  %-34s %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }' "$SITES.exempt"
239	fi
240	echo "  by file:"
241	awk -F'\t' '{ split($2, p, ":"); f[p[1]] += $1 } END { for (k in f) printf "%d\t%s\n", f[k], k }' "$SITES" \
242	    | sort -rn | awk 'NR <= 10 { printf "    %5d  %s\n", $1, $2 }'
243	
244	# The tier runner buffers a passing test's output, so the Linux number — the
245	# one the ratchet is set from — would be invisible in CI. Write the census where
246	# CI can carry it: the job summary, and a file the e2e job uploads as an
247	# artifact (test.yml: fork-budget-census.txt under RUNNER_TEMP).
248	_fb_census() {
249	    printf '### fork budget: %s external execs (budget %s) across %s source files\n\n```\n' "$_total" "$FORK_BUDGET" "$_files"
250	    awk -F'\t' 'NR <= 15 { printf "%5d  %-34s %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }' "$SITES"
251	    printf '```\n'
252	}
253	if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]] && { [[ -w "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" ]] || [[ ! -e "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" && -w "$(dirname "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY")" ]]; }; then
254	    _fb_census >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
255	fi
256	if [[ -n "${RUNNER_TEMP:-}" && -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/nonexistent}" ]]; then
257	    _fb_census > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fork-budget-census.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
258	fi
259	
260	if (( _files >= 20 && _total >= 1000 )); then
261	    assert_pass "[SPEC-3] the trace is live (${_files} files, ${_total} execs)"
262	else
263	    assert_fail "[SPEC-3] the trace is live" "only ${_files} files / ${_total} execs — fd 7 lost, or the run died early"
264	fi
265	# The pool's own execs scale with the work units it runs (the fixture dispatches
266	# 2), never with how long they take: its poll sleep is exempt, and no counted
267	# pool line runs more than once per unit.
268	if grep -qE $'\tlocal_engine\\.sh:[0-9]+\tsleep$' "$SITES.exempt" 2>/dev/null; then
269	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the worker pool's poll sleep is listed as an exempt wait"
270	else
271	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the worker pool's poll sleep is listed as an exempt wait" "exempt: $(cat "$SITES.exempt" 2>/dev/null)"
272	fi
273	_pool_max="$(awk -F'\t' '$2 ~ /^local_engine\.sh:/ && $1 > m { m = $1 } END { print m + 0 }' "$SITES")"
274	echo "  busiest counted pool line: ${_pool_max} execs (2 work units)"
275	assert_eq "[SPEC-6] …and no counted pool line runs more than once per work unit (max ${_pool_max})" "1" "$(( _pool_max <= 2 ))"
276	if (( _total <= FORK_BUDGET )); then
277	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] ${_total} external execs ≤ FORK_BUDGET ${FORK_BUDGET}"
278	else

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# E2E (#2151, ADR-065): the engine's process count is a tested contract.
#
# The suite is fork-bound — #1840 run 1 spent 4,910 of 6,989 CPU-seconds in the
# kernel creating processes — which is why it takes ~15 min on a 10-core Mac
# and ~58 min in the daemon's test stage on a 4-vCPU runner. A mocked 7-stage
# run execs ~6,600 external processes; `source runner.sh` alone execs 1,375.
#
# This test runs the mocked full pipeline (the parity fixture, the same launch
# as plugin-event-balance-full-run-test.sh) under bash xtrace and counts every
# external command the engine and its children exec. The count must stay under
# FORK_BUDGET, which only ratchets DOWN (raising it needs an ADR-065 amendment).
# The failure output IS the diagnosis: the top call sites and per-file totals.
#
# SPEC-1: a canary script with exactly one external exec counts exactly 1 — the
#         detector cannot go inert.
# SPEC-1b: the words inside an assigned value (xtrace quotes them) are data,
#          never commands (#1842).
# SPEC-2: the mocked run still exits 0 under tracing and writes events.jsonl.
# SPEC-3: liveness floor — the trace names ≥ 20 source files and ≥ 1,000
#         external execs (an fd-7-closed child traces to stderr; a run that died
#         early must not pass as "under budget").
# SPEC-4: total external execs ≤ FORK_BUDGET.
# SPEC-5: a line marked `# fork-budget-exempt: <why>` is not counted (listed
#         apart instead); an unmarked line in the same loop still is (#2236).
#         How often a wait loop sleeps measures elapsed time, not code — under
#         load the same tree counted 4,528 and 4,610.
# SPEC-6: the worker pool's execs scale with its work units, not with how long
#         they take: its poll sleep is exempt, and no counted pool line runs
#         more than once per unit (#2236).
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "fork budget: external execs of a mocked full run (#2151, ADR-065)"
setup_test_env "fork-budget"

# ADR-065 §2. Ratchets down only. History: 8000 (#2151, measured 7,128 macOS);
# 4800 (#2152 manifest index, measured 4,335 macOS); 4600 (#1849 follow-up:
# _eb_strip_ansi skips sed when no ESC byte is present — measured 4,187 macOS
# with the issue-acceptance stage added); 4550 (#2236: the pool's poll wait is
# exempt and its clock read a builtin — measured 4,499 macOS, the same under load).
# 6340 (#1842, ADR-065 §2 amendment): the fixture now runs what production runs —
# a real mock repo (hydrate, build's diff, persist's snapshot used to fail fast),
# and review_lenses -> review-aggregator -> pr. Measured 6,280 macOS; the same
# counter on main's fixture reads 4,367 (132 phantom execs in quoted values are
# gone, SPEC-1b). The biggest new site is persist's per-file git, #2249.
# 5740 (#2249): persist stages a snapshot in two git calls instead of two per
# file, and the fixture's git plumbing is real so snapshots actually save —
# measured 5,685 macOS (artifact-persist.sh 1,072 → 305).
# 5540 (#1844): a v2 result is read with one jq instead of eight
# (verdict.sh _verdict_read_result) — measured 5,481 macOS, even though design,
# pr-open and pr-delivery are now read as v2 (their results became primary).
# 5480 (#2271): the per-stage owner and fault lookups in the summary collector
# are gone with fault routing, which more than pays for numbered findings and
# answers — measured 5,426 macOS (Linux CI census 5,276).
# 4500 (#1806/SPEC-6): payload accumulation (single jq call per emit, not one
# per key=val arg) and sql-escape fixes eliminate per-arg forks from every
# eb_emit_event call.
FORK_BUDGET=4500

# ─── the trace harness (the --coverage-trace precedent, scripts/run-tests.sh) ──
# BASH_ENV injects `set -x` into every child bash (the runner, the mocks, work
# units); PS4 stamps source:line; BASH_XTRACEFD=7 routes it to one file. fd 3 is
# stage-io, 8 is coverage, 9 is flock — 7 is free (run-tests.sh:101-118).
_FB_BASH_ENV="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bashenv"
printf 'set -x\n' > "$_FB_BASH_ENV"
# Usage: _fb_traced <trace_file> <cmd...> — runs cmd with tracing to trace_file.
_fb_traced() {
    local trace="$1"; shift
    (
        export PS4='+@${BASH_SOURCE[0]-}:${LINENO}@ '
        export BASH_XTRACEFD=7
        export BASH_ENV="$_FB_BASH_ENV"
        "$@" 7>"$trace"
    )
}

# ─── the counter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _fb_count <trace_file> <sites_out>
# Prints the number of external execs; writes `count<TAB>file:line<TAB>cmd`
# rows (descending) to sites_out. A word is external when the TEST shell
# resolves it to a file on PATH (engine functions are not sourced here, so a
# function named like nothing on PATH is not counted), or it is one of the
# fixture's mocks. Leading `VAR=val` words and wrappers (exec, command, env,
# nice, timeout N) are stripped so the wrapped command is classified — and the
# wrapper counted too when it is itself a binary.
# A source line marked `# fork-budget-exempt: <why>` is a wait whose repeat count
# is elapsed time, not code (#2236): its rows go to <sites_out>.exempt instead.
_fb_count() {
    local trace="$1" sites="$2"
    local pairs="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pairs.$$" exempt="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/exempt.$$"
    # The marked lines of every traced source file, as `path:line`.
    : > "$exempt"
    local src
    while IFS= read -r src; do
        [[ -f "$src" ]] || continue
        grep -n 'fork-budget-exempt:' "$src" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: -v p="$src" '{ print p ":" $1 }' >> "$exempt" || true
    done < <(awk '/^\++@[^@]*@ /{ s = $0; sub(/^\++@/, "", s); sub(/:[0-9]*@ .*$/, "", s); if (!(s in seen)) { seen[s] = 1; print s } }' "$trace")
    # pass 1: one `site<TAB>word` row per candidate command word (no forks per line);
    # an exempt site's row is tagged so pass 2 lists it apart.
    awk -v exf="$exempt" '
        BEGIN { while ((getline l < exf) > 0) ex[l] = 1 }
        /^\++@[^@]*@ / {
            site = $0; sub(/^\++@/, "", site); sub(/@ .*$/, "", site)
            tag = (site in ex) ? "\tX" : ""
            n = split(site, sp, "/"); site = sp[n]
            line = $0; sub(/^\++@[^@]*@ /, "", line)
            m = split(line, w, " ")
            for (i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
                t = w[i]
                if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/) {                  # VAR=val prefix
                    # xtrace single-quotes a value with spaces (v=<q>a b c<q>,
                    # q = 0x27). Its words are data: skip to the closing quote.
                    v = t; sub(/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/, "", v)
                    if (v ~ /^\$?\x27/ && !(length(v) > 1 && v ~ /\x27$/ && v !~ /^\$?\x27$/)) {
                        while (i < m && w[i] !~ /\x27$/) i++
                        if (w[i] !~ /\x27$/) i++
                    }
                    continue
                }
                if (t == "exec" || t == "command" || t == "env" || t == "nice") continue
                # `timeout N cmd` is two processes — timeout forks cmd so it can
                # kill it — so both are counted (one row each), and N is skipped.
                if ((t == "timeout" || t == "gtimeout") && i < m) { print site "\t" t tag; i++; continue }
                gsub(/^[\x27"]|[\x27"]$/, "", t)
                print site "\t" t tag
                break
            }
        }' "$trace" > "$pairs"
    # classify each unique word once in this shell
    local w kind; local -A ext=()
    for w in claude gh git rsync; do ext["$w"]=1; done
    while IFS= read -r w; do
        [[ -n "$w" && -z "${ext[$w]+x}" ]] || continue
        kind="$(type -t -- "$w" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        [[ "$kind" == "file" ]] && ext["$w"]=1
    done < <(cut -f2 "$pairs" | sort -u)
    # pass 2: keep external rows, tally by site. The site table goes through a
    # temp file and a synchronous sort — a `2> >(sort …)` process substitution
    # would return before sort finished writing (review on #2153).
    local extlist=""; for w in "${!ext[@]}"; do extlist+="$w "; done
    local unsorted="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sites-unsorted.$$"
    awk -v extlist="$extlist" -v out="$unsorted" -v xout="$unsorted.x" '
        BEGIN { n = split(extlist, a, " "); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) ext[a[i]] = 1 }
        BEGIN { FS = "\t" }
        ($2 in ext) && $3 == "X" { xsite[$1 "\t" $2]++; next }
        ($2 in ext) { total++; site[$1 "\t" $2]++ }
        END {
            printf "" > out; printf "" > xout
            for (k in site) printf "%d\t%s\n", site[k], k > out
            for (k in xsite) printf "%d\t%s\n", xsite[k], k > xout
            close(out); close(xout)
            print total + 0
        }' "$pairs"
    sort -rn "$unsorted" > "$sites" 2>/dev/null || : > "$sites"
    sort -rn "$unsorted.x" > "$sites.exempt" 2>/dev/null || : > "$sites.exempt"
    rm -f "$pairs" "$unsorted" "$unsorted.x" "$exempt"
}

# ─── SPEC-1: the canary ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-1: a script with one external exec counts exactly 1"
CANARY="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/canary.sh"
cat > "$CANARY" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
x="$(dirname /a/b)"
y="${x%/*}"
printf '%s\n' "$y" >/dev/null
EOF
_fb_traced "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/canary.trace" bash "$CANARY"
_canary_n="$(_fb_count "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/canary.trace" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/canary.sites")"
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] the canary's one dirname is counted, its builtins are not" "1" "$_canary_n"
assert_contains "[SPEC-1] …and attributed to its call site" "$(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/canary.sites")" "canary.sh:2"$'\t'"dirname"

# ─── SPEC-1b: an assignment's value is not a command ─────────────────────────
# xtrace prints `v='review lens: security'` for an assignment whose value has
# spaces. The words inside the quotes are data; `security` is a binary on macOS,
# and 178 phantom execs per site were counted from such values (#1842).
QUOTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/quoted.sh"
cat > "$QUOTED" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
v="first ls second"
w='x cat y'
z=$'a\tmkdir b'
EOF
_fb_traced "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/quoted.trace" bash "$QUOTED"
assert_eq "[SPEC-1b] words inside an assigned value are not counted" "0" \
    "$(_fb_count "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/quoted.trace" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/quoted.sites")"

# ─── SPEC-5: an exempt wait is listed, not counted ───────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-5: a marked wait is not counted"
WAITER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/waiter.sh"
cat > "$WAITER" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for _ in 1 2 3; do
    sleep 0  # fork-budget-exempt: canary wait
    sleep 0
done
EOF
_fb_traced "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/waiter.trace" bash "$WAITER"
_waiter_n="$(_fb_count "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/waiter.trace" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/waiter.sites")"
assert_eq "[SPEC-5] only the unmarked sleep is counted (3 of 6)" "3" "$_waiter_n"
assert_contains "[SPEC-5] …the marked one is listed apart" \
    "$(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/waiter.sites.exempt" 2>/dev/null)" "waiter.sh:3"$'\t'"sleep"

# ─── SPEC-2: the mocked full run under tracing ───────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-2: the mocked full run under tracing"
FIXTURE="$REPO_ROOT/tests/golden/parity/run-fixture.sh"
RUN_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/run"; BIN_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/events" "$BIN_DIR" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pc"
TRACE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/run.trace"
set +e
(
    unset GITHUB_ACTIONS CI GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY RUNNER_OS 2>/dev/null || true
    export FIXTURE_STATE_DIR="$RUN_DIR" FIXTURE_BIN_DIR="$BIN_DIR" ZBUILD_PLAN_CONTEXT_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pc"
    _fb_traced "$TRACE" bash "$FIXTURE" >/dev/null 2>&1
)
_run_rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "[SPEC-2] the mocked full run exits 0 under tracing" "0" "$_run_rc"
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] …and produced events.jsonl" "$RUN_DIR/events/events.jsonl"

# ─── SPEC-3/4: the count ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-3/4: liveness floor and the budget"
SITES="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/run.sites"
_total="$(_fb_count "$TRACE" "$SITES")"
_files="$(awk -F'\t' '{ split($2, p, ":"); f[p[1]] = 1 } END { print length(f) }' "$SITES")"
echo "  external execs: $_total (budget $FORK_BUDGET) across $_files source files"
echo "  top call sites:"
awk -F'\t' 'NR <= 12 { printf "    %5d  %-34s %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }' "$SITES"
if [[ -s "$SITES.exempt" ]]; then
    echo "  exempt waits (not counted — their repeat count is elapsed time):"
    awk -F'\t' '{ printf "    %5d  %-34s %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }' "$SITES.exempt"
fi
echo "  by file:"
awk -F'\t' '{ split($2, p, ":"); f[p[1]] += $1 } END { for (k in f) printf "%d\t%s\n", f[k], k }' "$SITES" \
    | sort -rn | awk 'NR <= 10 { printf "    %5d  %s\n", $1, $2 }'

# The tier runner buffers a passing test's output, so the Linux number — the
# one the ratchet is set from — would be invisible in CI. Write the census where
# CI can carry it: the job summary, and a file the e2e job uploads as an
# artifact (test.yml: fork-budget-census.txt under RUNNER_TEMP).
_fb_census() {
    printf '### fork budget: %s external execs (budget %s) across %s source files\n\n```\n' "$_total" "$FORK_BUDGET" "$_files"
    awk -F'\t' 'NR <= 15 { printf "%5d  %-34s %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }' "$SITES"
    printf '```\n'
}
if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]] && { [[ -w "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" ]] || [[ ! -e "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" && -w "$(dirname "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY")" ]]; }; then
    _fb_census >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi
if [[ -n "${RUNNER_TEMP:-}" && -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/nonexistent}" ]]; then
    _fb_census > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fork-budget-census.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if (( _files >= 20 && _total >= 1000 )); then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-3] the trace is live (${_files} files, ${_total} execs)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-3] the trace is live" "only ${_files} files / ${_total} execs — fd 7 lost, or the run died early"
fi
# The pool's own execs scale with the work units it runs (the fixture dispatches
# 2), never with how long they take: its poll sleep is exempt, and no counted
# pool line runs more than once per unit.
if grep -qE $'\tlocal_engine\\.sh:[0-9]+\tsleep$' "$SITES.exempt" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the worker pool's poll sleep is listed as an exempt wait"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the worker pool's poll sleep is listed as an exempt wait" "exempt: $(cat "$SITES.exempt" 2>/dev/null)"
fi
_pool_max="$(awk -F'\t' '$2 ~ /^local_engine\.sh:/ && $1 > m { m = $1 } END { print m + 0 }' "$SITES")"
echo "  busiest counted pool line: ${_pool_max} execs (2 work units)"
assert_eq "[SPEC-6] …and no counted pool line runs more than once per work unit (max ${_pool_max})" "1" "$(( _pool_max <= 2 ))"
if (( _total <= FORK_BUDGET )); then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] ${_total} external execs ≤ FORK_BUDGET ${FORK_BUDGET}"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] external execs ≤ FORK_BUDGET" "${_total} > ${FORK_BUDGET} — see the call sites above; ADR-065 §2: the budget only ratchets down"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
3	# ║  zBuild event-bus — emit_event with dual SQLite + JSONL writers           ║
4	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
5	#
6	# Single-writer JSONL (flock-guarded) + optional SQLite mirror for durability.
7	# Schema-as-warn: unknown event types log a warning but never block.
8	# Events from ARCHITECTURE.md §6.
9	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
10	
11	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
12	_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_LOADED=1
13	
14	_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
15	_ZBUILD_ROOT_FOR_EVENTS="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
16	
17	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/compat.sh
18	source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT_FOR_EVENTS/scripts/lib/compat.sh"
19	# The known-type set (#1717): engine config + every manifest's provides.events.
20	# shellcheck source=known-types.sh
21	source "$_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_DIR/known-types.sh"
22	
23	# ─── Locations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
24	# An engine run (core/pipeline/runner.sh) ALWAYS pins these to its per-run dir
25	# (runs/<run_id>/, #887). An UNPINNED caller — an ad-hoc/test invocation that
26	# sources the event-bus directly — must NOT accumulate into the shared
27	# ${HOME}/.zbuild/state/events.{jsonl,db}: that store grows unbounded across
28	# ad-hoc invocations and a stale events.jsonl.lock left by a killed run can
29	# hang a later run's `flock -w` (#run-hygiene). Resolve the defaults coherently:
30	#   1. Nothing pinned  → ephemeral, process-scoped dir under the DATA ROOT,
31	#      never the durable shared global default and never ${TMPDIR}. ADR-059 §1
32	#      makes the path the keying: a reclaimer deletes a `runs/<id>/` or an
33	#      `issues/<N>/` and the scope follows from where it sits, so a ${TMPDIR}
34	#      default is outside every reclaimable path by construction — which is why
35	#      cleanup.sh needed a ZBUILD_TMPDIR_PATTERNS scanner to sweep ~2300 of
36	#      these (#2004). ADR-023/ADR-059 §1 also reject ${TMPDIR} for durable
37	#      state: on macOS its entries can vanish mid-run (#1571, #1609/#1611).
38	#   2. Only JSONL pinned → derive the dir (hence the SQLite mirror + lock) from
39	#      it, so a pinned jsonl never leaks a mirror/lock back to the global
40	#      default (the test harness pins only ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL).
41	# Explicit ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR / _DB always win.
42	if [[ -z "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-}${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-}${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB:-}" ]]; then
43	    # Same precedence as zbuild_layout_data_root (core/state/layout.sh); inlined
44	    # because the event bus deliberately sources almost nothing.
45	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="${ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.zbuild}}/ephemeral-events/$$"
46	elif [[ -z "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-}" && -n "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-}" ]]; then
47	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$(dirname "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL")"
48	fi
49	ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-${HOME}/.zbuild/state}}"
50	ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR}/events.jsonl}"
51	ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB:-${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR}/events.db}"
52	ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="${ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT_FOR_EVENTS}/config/event-schema.json}"
53	
54	# ─── _eb_mirror_enabled — is the optional SQLite mirror active? ─────────────
55	# True only when sqlite3 is installed AND a real DB path is configured.
56	# ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB=/dev/null is the "JSONL only, no mirror" sentinel (parity
57	# fixtures use it); its `.lock` path is unwritable, so the mirror — including
58	# the dedicated lock — must be skipped entirely, not just fail-soft (#1153).
59	_eb_mirror_enabled() {
60	    [[ "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" != "/dev/null" ]] && command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1
61	}
62	
63	# _eb_host_is_mac — true when the host OS is macOS, regardless of ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
64	# Uses $OSTYPE (bash builtin, zero forks) so map work units exporting
65	# ZBUILD_PLATFORM=linux on a macOS host get the correct date format.
66	_eb_host_is_mac() { [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; }
67	
68	# ─── _eb_init — idempotent setup (dir, lockfile, SQLite schema) ─────────────
69	_eb_init() {
70	    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
71	    : > "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL}.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
72	    # SQLite mirror (optional, best-effort) — set up the dedicated mirror lock
73	    # (SEPARATE from the jsonl lock, so a slow mirror never blocks the
74	    # authoritative append, #1153) and schema only when the mirror is enabled.
75	    if _eb_mirror_enabled; then
76	        : > "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB}.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
77	      if [[ ! -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" ]]; then
78	        local _eb_init_err
79	        # busy_timeout via -cmd (no stdout echo, unlike PRAGMA busy_timeout=N).
80	        # Concurrent mirror writes are serialized by flock (ADR-005) in
81	        # eb_emit_event — flock is the deterministic primitive zbuild requires,
82	        # whereas sqlite3 is optional. The timeout is just a cheap safety net
83	        # for a stale lock holder (#1059 chose 2000ms). The mirror stays in the
84	        # default journal mode: no concurrent reader of events.db exists (jsonl
85	        # is the only read path, via eb_query_events).
86	        _eb_init_err="$(sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 2000" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" <<'SQL' 2>&1
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
88	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
89	    ts TEXT NOT NULL,
90	    run_id TEXT,
91	    issue INTEGER,
92	    type TEXT NOT NULL,
93	    plugin TEXT,
94	    kind TEXT,
95	    payload TEXT,
96	    schema_version INTEGER DEFAULT 1
97	);
98	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_ts ON events(ts);
99	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_type ON events(type);
100	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_run_id ON events(run_id);
101	SQL
102	        )" || { [[ -n "$_eb_init_err" ]] && echo "[event-bus] WARN: sqlite3 failed: $_eb_init_err" >&2; }
103	      fi
104	    fi
105	}
106	
107	# ─── _eb_known_type — schema-as-warn check ──────────────────────────────────
108	# Returns 0 if known, 1 if unknown (but never blocks emission).
109	#
110	# #1717: this used to fork `jq` against ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA on EVERY emit. The
111	# known set now also spans every plugin manifest, so per-emit reading would have
112	# multiplied that fork by plugin count. Composition happens once (per process,
113	# and once per RUN via the file cache in known-types.sh); the check itself is an
114	# associative-array lookup and forks nothing.
115	_eb_known_type() {
116	    eb_known_types_has "$1"
117	}
118	
119	# _eb_strip_ansi — strip CSI + bare-ESC sequences from a string before JSONL emission.
120	# Ported from legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/helpers.sh:431-437; two-pass form mirrors _stage_io_strip_ansi.
121	# LC_ALL=C so sed processes raw bytes without aborting on non-UTF-8 sequences (issue #830).
122	# No ESC byte → nothing to strip, and no fork: this runs for every value of every
123	# event, and a sed per call was the single largest exec site in a run (ADR-065).
124	_eb_strip_ansi() {
125	    [[ "$1" == *$'\x1b'* ]] || { printf '%s' "$1"; return 0; }
126	    printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sed -E $'s/\x1b\\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z~]//g; s/\x1b.//g'
127	}
128	
129	# ─── eb_emit_event — single source of truth for events ──────────────────────
130	# Usage:
131	#   eb_emit_event <type> [key1=val1] [key2=val2] ...
132	#
133	# Standard envelope fields are picked up from env vars:
134	#   ZBUILD_RUN_ID, ZBUILD_ISSUE, ZBUILD_PLUGIN, ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND
135	eb_emit_event() {
136	    local type="$1"; shift
137	    _eb_init
138	
139	    if ! _eb_known_type "$type"; then
140	        # Schema-as-warn: always log, never block.
141	        echo "[event-bus] WARN: unknown event type '$type' (run_id=${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-})" >&2
142	    fi
143	
144	    # Build payload from key=val args. plugin/kind are also captured here as a
145	    # fallback for the envelope (#1705): emitters outside plugin_hook_call's
146	    # dynamic extent — the contract checker, the tamper check — never see the
147	    # exported ZBUILD_PLUGIN context, and left the envelope's advertised
148	    # .plugin/.kind empty. Captured in this existing loop so the hot path gains
149	    # no subprocess, and applied below only when the exported context is absent.
150	    local _data_plugin="" _data_kind=""
151	    local -a _jq_args=()
152	    local key val
153	    for arg in "$@"; do
154	        key="${arg%%=*}"
155	        val="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${arg#*=}")"
156	        case "$key" in
157	            plugin) _data_plugin="$val" ;;
158	            kind)   _data_kind="$val" ;;
159	        esac
160	        _jq_args+=(--arg "$key" "$val")
161	    done
162	    local payload
163	    if [[ ${#_jq_args[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
164	        payload="{}"
165	    else
166	        payload="$(jq -n '$ARGS.named' "${_jq_args[@]}")"
167	    fi
168	
169	    # ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds
170	    local ts
171	    if _eb_host_is_mac; then
172	        ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z)"
173	    else
174	        ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3NZ)"
175	    fi
176	
177	    local run_id; run_id="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}")"
178	    local issue="${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}"
179	    local plugin; plugin="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_PLUGIN:-}")"
180	    local kind; kind="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND:-}")"
181	    # Fall back to the payload's own plugin/kind so the envelope is populated
182	    # for every emitter, not only those dispatched through plugin_hook_call.
183	    # Applied before the SQLite insert too, so both stores agree.
184	    if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then plugin="$_data_plugin"; fi
185	    if [[ -z "$kind" ]]; then kind="$_data_kind"; fi
186	    # ADR-004 / ADR-039 §3: stamp the active stage onto the envelope so the
187	    # router's C6 precondition can be scoped PER-STAGE. Parallel-group members
188	    # (parallel-orchestrator.sh) each export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE inside their
189	    # own subshell, so a sibling member's `plugin.run.start` can no longer
190	    # become the most-recent event that satisfies/clobbers THIS member's
191	    # `redaction.applied` check. Present ONLY when a stage is active — stage-less
192	    # emits (pipeline.start, template load, bootstrap) keep the canonical 8-key
193	    # envelope, so C6 falls back to the run-level last-event check for them.
194	    local stage; stage="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}")"
195	    # #2131 (ADR-064): the stage-io seq label (`6.1.3` = runner cardinal ·
196	    # cycle iteration · member position) rides the envelope by the same rule
197	    # as `stage` — present only while a label is exported. It was rendered
198	    # into the banner and persisted nowhere, so the run-status comment had no
199	    # key to pair a stage's start with its end. Validated, not ANSI-stripped:
200	    # the label is engine-generated digits and dots, and anything else is an
201	    # upstream fault that must not become a row key downstream.
202	    local seq="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_SEQ_LABEL:-}"
203	    [[ "$seq" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$ ]] || seq=""
204	    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): a map member's own name rides the envelope only
205	    # when it differs from the stage, so every other envelope is unchanged.
206	    local unit="${ZBUILD_UNIT:-}"
207	    [[ "$unit" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+){0,2}$ && "$unit" != "$stage" ]] || unit=""
208	
209	    # Validate-or-cast $issue to a non-negative integer. Coming from env, an
210	    # unsanitized string here would break the SQL INSERT below ($issue is
211	    # interpolated unquoted because the column is INTEGER).
212	    if ! [[ "$issue" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
213	        issue=0
214	    fi
215	
216	    local event_json
217	    event_json="$(jq -cn \
218	        --arg ts "$ts" \
219	        --arg run_id "$run_id" \
220	        --argjson issue "$issue" \
221	        --arg type "$type" \
222	        --arg plugin "$plugin" \
223	        --arg kind "$kind" \
224	        --arg stage "$stage" \
225	        --arg seq "$seq" \
226	        --arg unit "$unit" \
227	        --argjson data "$payload" \
228	        '{ts: $ts, run_id: $run_id, issue: $issue, type: $type, plugin: $plugin, kind: $kind, data: $data, schema_version: 1}
229	         + (if $stage != "" then {stage: $stage} else {} end)
230	         + (if $seq != "" then {seq: $seq} else {} end)
231	         + (if $unit != "" then {unit: $unit} else {} end)')"
232	
233	    # Single-writer JSONL via flock
234	    if zbuild_has_flock; then
235	        (
236	            flock -w 5 9 || exit 1
237	            echo "$event_json" >> "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
238	        ) 9>"${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL}.lock"
239	    else
240	        # Best-effort fallback
241	        echo "$event_json" >> "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
242	    fi
243	
244	    # SQLite mirror (optional, fire-and-forget).
245	    # Escape every string field — previously only $payload was escaped, so a
246	    # plugin emitting e.g. ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND="x'); DROP TABLE events;--"
247	    # could corrupt the event store. $issue is validated as integer above
248	    # and interpolated unquoted (INTEGER column). Skipped (incl. the flock on
249	    # the dedicated lock) when the mirror is disabled — e.g. ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB=
250	    # /dev/null, whose .lock redirect would otherwise fail the emit (#1153).
251	    if _eb_mirror_enabled; then
252	        local _ts_esc _rid_esc _type_esc _plugin_esc _kind_esc _payload_esc
253	        _ts_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$ts")"
254	        _rid_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$run_id")"
255	        _type_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$type")"
256	        _plugin_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$plugin")"
257	        _kind_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$kind")"
258	        _payload_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$payload")"
259	        local _eb_insert_sql
260	        _eb_insert_sql="INSERT INTO events (ts, run_id, issue, type, plugin, kind, payload, schema_version) VALUES ('$_ts_esc', '$_rid_esc', $issue, '$_type_esc', '$_plugin_esc', '$_kind_esc', '$_payload_esc', 1);"
261	        # Serialize the mirror INSERT with flock on the DEDICATED db lock (NOT
262	        # the jsonl lock): flock is the deterministic primitive zbuild requires
263	        # (ADR-005), so concurrent emitters (#1131) never collide on the mirror
264	        # write. NON-BLOCKING (-n): if another emitter holds the lock, SKIP this
265	        # best-effort mirror write rather than wait — the mirror is unread
266	        # (events.jsonl is the only read path) so a dropped row is harmless,
267	        # and never waiting means a high-emit-rate pipeline (parallel members,
268	        # kill-mid-run tests) pays ZERO added latency for the mirror. Separate
269	        # lock ⇒ the mirror can never block the authoritative jsonl append.
270	        if zbuild_has_flock; then
271	            (
272	                flock -n 9 || exit 0
273	                _eb_mirror_insert "$_eb_insert_sql"
274	            ) 9>"${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB}.lock"
275	        else
276	            _eb_mirror_insert "$_eb_insert_sql"
277	        fi
278	    fi
279	
280	    # Fire-and-forget: emit MUST never fail its caller — eb_emit_event is called
281	    # bare under `set -e` throughout the pipeline, so the best-effort mirror's
282	    # rc (or a flock-block rc) must not become this function's rc. Without this
283	    # the trailing mirror block's exit code propagated out and aborted stages
284	    # (build:fail / test:error) when the INSERT returned non-zero (#1153 fix).
285	    return 0
286	}
287	
288	# _eb_mirror_insert — run one best-effort mirror INSERT; warn (never fail) on
289	# sqlite3 error. Caller serializes via flock. busy_timeout via -cmd (no stdout,
290	# unlike PRAGMA busy_timeout=N which echoes the value) is a safety net for a
291	# stale lock holder (#1059 chose the 2000ms window).
292	_eb_mirror_insert() {
293	    local _eb_emit_err
294	    _eb_emit_err="$(sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 2000" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" "$1" 2>&1)" \
295	        || { [[ -n "$_eb_emit_err" ]] && echo "[event-bus] WARN: sqlite3 failed: $_eb_emit_err" >&2; }
296	}
297	
298	# _eb_sql_escape: double single-quotes for SQLite single-quoted string literals.
299	# Single source of truth; used for every string field in the INSERT above.
300	# $'...' ANSI-C quoting avoids the double-quote context issue (#278) where
301	# ${s//\'/\'\'} would produce literal backslash+quote instead of two quotes.
302	_eb_sql_escape() {
303	    printf '%s' "${1//$'\''/$'\'\''}"
304	}
305	
306	# ─── eb_query_events — minimal read API ─────────────────────────────────────
307	# Usage: eb_query_events [type_filter] [limit]
308	eb_query_events() {
309	    local type_filter="${1:-}"
310	    local limit="${2:-100}"
311	    if [[ ! -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
312	        return 0
313	    fi
314	    if [[ -n "$type_filter" ]]; then
315	        jq -c --arg t "$type_filter" 'select(.type == $t)' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" | tail -"$limit"
316	    else
317	        tail -"$limit" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
318	    fi
319	}
320	
321	# ─── Override emit_event from helpers.sh ────────────────────────────────────
322	# The placeholder emit_event in scripts/lib/helpers.sh delegates here when
323	# the event-bus is sourced. Just redefine the function.
324	emit_event() {
325	    eb_emit_event "$@"
326	}
